title: Counting maps to UT3(F4) x| C3 is #P-hard with H1 = Z/3
claim: Let G = UT3(F4) x| C3 (action (w^2 x, w^2 y, w z); order 192, Fitting height 2). Counting homomorphisms from pi1(S^3_3(K)) to G, for knots K given by diagrams, is #P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions with one oracle call; every such manifold has H1 = Z/3. Gadget: for a graph with n vertices and m edges, the alternating form A = sum over edges uv of (x_u + x_v) ^ p_e ^ q_e on F4^{n+2m} has kernel count N(A) = 4^{2m-n} Z(64, 15), where Z(q, v) = sum over maps s from vertices to q colours of the product over edges of (1 + v [s(u) = s(v)]) is the Potts partition function; Z(64, 15) = 64^k 15^{n-k} T(79/15, 16), with k components and T the Tutte polynomial, which is #P-hard to evaluate (Jaeger-Vertigan-Welsh; Vertigan for planar graphs) because (79/15 - 1)(16 - 1) = 64. Realization: starting from 3-surgery on a connected sum of n + 2m figure-eight knots (V = F4^{n+2m}, T = 0), one Borromean move per edge, with leaves a band sum of the vertex loops and the two edge loops, gives a knot K_G with T = A and |Hom(pi1 S^3_3(K_G), G)| = 1 + 128 4^{n+2m} 4^{2m-n} Z(64, 15). So with bounded first homology, a group of Fitting height 2 can be #P-hard, while SL(2,3) is polynomial.
failure_conditions: A graph on which the brute-force kernel count of the gadget differs from 4^{2m-n} Z(64, 15), or Z(64, 15) differs from the Tutte expression.
An end-to-end knot built from figure-eight summands and Borromean insertions realizing a cycle configuration whose count differs from the gadget value.
A figure-eight connected sum with nonzero triple product or with dim V different from the number of summands.
A control that cannot fail: an unbalanced realization of a cycle (gains with product not 1) must give a different count.
foundation_claim_scope: 3-surgeries on knots in the 3-sphere (closed 3-manifolds with H1 = Z/3), given by knot diagrams; Turing reductions with one oracle call. Cited, not proved: the #P-hardness of Tutte evaluation off the hyperbola (x-1)(y-1) = 1 (Jaeger-Vertigan-Welsh 1990; Vertigan 2005 for planar graphs), Habiro's clasper calculus for drawing the moves, and the results cited by TRIPLE-PRODUCT-20261026-001A and 001C. Checked: the gadget formula by brute force over F2 and F4, and end-to-end on knots realizing a triangle and a digon. Hardness of exact counting only; no claim about approximate counting, decision versions, P versus NP, or physics.

validation.status: checked: the gadget lemma by brute force over F2 and F4 on five graphs with Potts and Tutte values, figure-eight sums up to nine summands, four end-to-end knots realizing a triangle and a digon, and a gain control; hardness via cited Jaeger-Vertigan-Welsh; no human or external review
